The City Council welcomes both written and oral public comment on items that appear on City and within the purview of the committee.

If you wish to request accessibility accommodations , please do so as soon as possible. Every effort will be made to accommodate each request.

You can email all nine Councilmembers by sending your comments to or contacting them individually.

Email Your Comments to All Councilmembers

The Seattle City Council is conducting its meetings in a hybrid setting, both virtually and in-person. You can provide oral comments in one of two ways:

  • Sign up using the form below. The form will be available one hour before the start of applicable Council meetings. Speakers must be registered in order to be recognized by the Chair. Registration will close once the meeting's public comment period has concluded. All information entered into this form is subject to public disclosure.
  • Please register with the phone number you will be calling from to ensure you are recognized.
  • An email message will be sent to the registered email address that includes the meeting call-in information and details.
  • Call the phone number to join the meeting at least 5 minutes before it begins
  • Speakers will be asked to provide comment in the order of registration. The Chair will call on each speaker by name, at which point they can unmute themselves pressing *6 on their phone and will then have up to 2 minutes to give public comment.

Register to speak on the public comment sign-up sheet located inside Council Chambers at least 15 minutes prior to the meeting. Registration will end at the conclusion of the public comment period during the meeting. Speakers must be registered in order to be recognized by the Chair.

  • Introduction and Referral Calendar items are listed on Full City Council agendas

Citywide Information

  1. Find Your District and Councilmembers

The Seattle City Council establishes City policy through enactment of ordinances (laws) and adoption of resolutions. The City Council also approves and adopts the City's budget. The nine Council members and their legislative assistants are part of the City of Seattle Legislative Department.
